cmd.root.short: Native filesystem for OneDrive on Linux
cmd.account.remove.long:
Removes a Microsoft account and, by default, asks whether to delete
its local cache (~/.cache/onecloudriver/<account>).

Use --purge to delete the cache without asking, or --keep to preserve it.
cmd.completion.short: Generate the autocompletion script for the specified shell
cmd.copy.short: Copy a file or folder in OneDrive
cmd.copy.long:
Copies an item (file or folder) to a new location and/or with a new name.

The copy operation is asynchronous and returns a URL to monitor progress.

The source is specified by --id or --path. Optionally you can specify:
  --name: new name for the copy
  --dest-id / --dest-path: destination folder

At least one of --name or --dest-* must be specified:

  onecloudriver copy --account user@mail.com --id 01BYE5RZ... --name "copy.pdf"
  onecloudriver copy --account user@mail.com --path /Docs/photo.jpg --dest-path /Backup
cmd.download.short: Download a file from OneDrive to local disk
cmd.download.long:
Downloads a file from OneDrive to local disk using streaming with support
for large files (>10 MB) via Range requests.

The file must be specified by ID or by path (not both), and the destination:

  onecloudriver download --account user@mail.com --id 01BYE5RZ... --output ./file.pdf
  onecloudriver download --account user@mail.com --path /Documents/photo.jpg -o ./photo.jpg
  onecloudriver download --account user@mail.com --id 01BYE5RZ... --output-dir ./downloads
cmd.info.short: Show detailed information about a OneDrive file or folder
cmd.info.long:
Displays the complete metadata of a DriveItem (file or folder) from OneDrive.

The item must be specified by ID or by path (not both):

  onecloudriver info --account user@mail.com --id 01BYE5RZ...
  onecloudriver info --account user@mail.com --path /Documents/photo.jpg
cmd.list.short: List the contents of a OneDrive folder (root by default)
cmd.list.long:
Lists the files and folders of a OneDrive folder.
With no flags it lists the root folder. Use --id or --path (not both) to
target an arbitrary folder:

  onecloudriver list --account user@mail.com --path /Documents
  onecloudriver list --account user@mail.com --id 01BYE5RZ...
cmd.mount.short: Mount OneDrive at the specified directory
cmd.mount.long:
Mounts OneDrive as a FUSE filesystem at the specified directory.

If no mountpoint is specified and the account has a saved defaultMountpoint
(from the last successful mount), it is reused automatically.

Configuration flags override the values persisted in the account JSON.
New values are automatically saved for the next session, except
--cache-dir, which is a session-only override and is never persisted.
cmd.mv.short: Move a file or folder to another location in OneDrive
cmd.rename.short: Rename a file or folder in OneDrive
cmd.rm.short: Permanently delete a file or folder from OneDrive
cmd.service.short: Manage the systemd service for auto-mount on login
cmd.service.long:
Installs, uninstalls and manages a user systemd service that
automatically mounts OneDrive on login.

The service is installed as a template (@.service), allowing
multiple accounts to be managed simultaneously:

  onecloudriver service install --account user@outlook.com --enable

Each instance mounts at ~/OneDrive/<account> (configurable with --mountpoint).
cmd.service.install.long:
Creates the systemd service file at ~/.config/systemd/user/onecloudriver@.service
and reloads the systemd daemon.

If --mountpoint is not specified, the defaultMountpoint from the account
JSON is reused only when it contains the %i instance placeholder. A concrete
saved mountpoint (no %i) is ignored, and ~/OneDrive/%i is used as fallback.

If --account is not specified and only ONE account is configured, it is
used automatically. With multiple accounts, --account is required.

With --enable, activates and starts the service automatically.

Examples:
  onecloudriver service install
  onecloudriver service install --mountpoint ~/OneDrive/%%i
  onecloudriver service install --mountpoint ~/OneDrive/%%i -a user@outlook.com --enable
cmd.service.uninstall.long:
Stops all active instances, disables the service
and removes the service file from ~/.config/systemd/user/.
cmd.service.status.short: Show service status (all accounts or a specific one)
cmd.service.start.short: Start the service for an account
cmd.service.stop.short: Stop the service and unmount the filesystem
cmd.service.stop.long:
Stops the systemd service and unmounts the FUSE filesystem
for the specified account.

With --all, stops and unmounts all configured accounts.

Unmounting is done both via systemd (ExecStop=fusermount3 -uz) and
with a direct fusermount3 call as fallback, ensuring the mountpoint
is freed even if systemd does not complete ExecStop.
cmd.sync.long:
Force an immediate delta synchronization for an account, independent of
the background poll interval of a mount.

Applies the remote changes (items created, modified or deleted from other
clients) to the account's persisted cache right now and prints how many
changes were applied. It works without a mount, reusing the same DeltaSync
machinery as the background loop.

A running mount already polls on its own schedule (--delta-interval) and holds
an exclusive lock on the account's cache, so run this while the account is not
mounted (or stop the mount/service first).
cmd.upload.short: Upload a local file to OneDrive
cmd.upload.long:
Uploads a file from the local disk to OneDrive.

For small files (≤4 MB) it uses a simple PUT request.
For large files (>4 MB) it uses upload sessions with 320 KiB chunks.

The destination folder is specified by ID or by path:

  onecloudriver upload --account user@mail.com --id FOLDER123 --file ./photo.jpg
  onecloudriver upload --account user@mail.com --path /Documents --file ./document.pdf
flag.lang: Language override (e.g. es, en). Default: system locale
flag.log.level: Minimum log level: trace, debug, info, warn, error
flag.log.json: Emit structured JSON logs to stderr (systemd/journal friendly)
flag.account: Account name to use. If omitted, uses the only configured account.
flag.etag: ETag of the item for concurrency control (optional)
flag.list.id: ID of the folder to list (default: root)
flag.list.path: Path of the folder to list (default: root, e.g.: /Documents)
flag.info.id: ID of the DriveItem to query
flag.info.path: Path of the DriveItem to query (e.g.: /Documents/photo.jpg)
flag.download.id: ID of the DriveItem to download
flag.download.path: Path of the DriveItem to download (e.g.: /Documents/photo.jpg)
flag.download.output: Local path where to save the downloaded file
flag.download.output.dir: Directory where to save the file with its original name
flag.mkdir.name: Name of the new folder (required)
flag.upload.file: Path of the local file to upload (required)
flag.rm.id: ID of the item to delete
flag.rm.path: Path of the item to delete (e.g.: /Documents/photo.jpg)
flag.rename.id: ID of the item to rename
flag.rename.path: Path of the item to rename (e.g.: /Documents/old.txt)
flag.rename.name: New name of the item (required)
flag.mv.id: ID of the item to move
flag.mv.path: Path of the item to move (e.g.: /Documents/old.txt)
flag.copy.id: ID of the item to copy
flag.copy.path: Path of the item to copy (e.g.: /Documents/photo.jpg)
flag.copy.name: New name for the copy
flag.account.purge: Delete the local cache without asking for confirmation
flag.account.keep: Preserve the local cache (do not delete it)
flag.mount.cache.dir: Root cache directory for THIS mount only; not saved to the account config (default: ~/.cache/onecloudriver/<account>)
flag.mount.cache.max.entries: Max folders with cached children in memory. 0 = use persisted or default
flag.mount.cache.max.size: Max ContentCache size on disk (e.g.: 1GB, 500MB). 0 = unlimited
flag.mount.max.uploads: Max concurrent uploads (default: 5). 0 = use persisted or default
flag.mount.upload.retries: Max retries per upload (default: 5). 0 = use persisted or default
flag.mount.graph.retries: HTTP retries on 429/503 (default: 3). 0 = use persisted or default
flag.mount.pre.warm.depth: Metadata pre-warm depth after mount (0=off, 1=root, 2=root+1, up to 10; default 2)
flag.mount.debug: Start a local expvar + pprof debug server (default 127.0.0.1:6060) and raise the log level to debug
flag.mount.debug.addr: Address for the --debug server (loopback by default; never expose on a public interface unless intended)
flag.service.mountpoint: Base mount path. Use %i for the placeholder. If omitted, uses the defaultMountpoint from account JSON or ~/OneDrive/%i
flag.service.account: Microsoft account to use. If omitted, uses the only configured account.
flag.service.enable: Enable and start the service immediately after installing it
flag.service.install.all: Install the service for ALL configured accounts
flag.service.stop.all: Stop the service for ALL configured accounts
flag.service.uninstall.all: Uninstall the service for ALL configured accounts
